title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the third draft of Grothendieck's axiomatic, point-free 'analysis situs'. M is a class of tame closed 'pieces' (think compact polyhedra or tame compact sets). The available relations are:
- ≤ : inclusion.
- ≪ : Y is a well-placed sub-piece of X. By the strengthened Axiom 1 on p.87, Y may meet ∂X, but only in a piece L ≪ ∂X, with Y∖L kept apart from ∂X.
- ‖ : 'apart' / disjoint, with ⊓ a meet-like operation (Z ⊓ ∂X = ∅).
- ∂X : the boundary piece.
- Omb(X) : the 'shadow' of X, i.e. the set of Z ≪ X.
- X̃ : a family attached to X, apparently pieces equivalent to or slightly modified from X, with Omb(X') ⊂ Omb(X) for X' in X̃.
- omb(X) : the points of X.

The page introduces the interior X° without points, as a family of pieces.
(i) Define Omb°°(X) = {Y ∈ Omb(X) : Y ‖ ∂X}, the sub-pieces lying strictly inside X. Clearly Omb°°(X) ⊂ Omb°(X) := Omb(X) ∖ Omb(∂X).
(ii) Define X° ‖ Y° to mean Omb°°(X) ∩ Omb°°(Y) = ∅. Equivalently, there is no Z with Z ≪ X, Z ≪ Y, Z ⊓ ∂X = ∅ and Z ⊓ ∂Y = ∅. A remark records that Z ≪ X, Y implies some Z' ∈ Z̃ satisfies Z' < X or Z' < Y.

Desired lemma: X ‖ Y ⇔ for all X' ∈ X̃ and Y' ∈ Ỹ, X'° ‖ Y'°. This expresses apartness of closed pieces through apartness of their interiors after small modification.
- ⇒ : X ‖ Y means no Z ≪ X, Y. Interior pieces of X', Y' lie in Omb(X), Omb(Y), so a fortiori no common one exists.
- ⇐ : flagged as more delicate. It is to follow from axioms 'L2, L3', which reduce ‖ to points: X ‖ Y ⇔ x ‖ y for all points x ∈ omb(X), y ∈ omb(Y).

The page breaks off there. On p.89 Grothendieck renames Omb°°(X) as X° and claims the lemma holds even without L2, L3. He then starts Lemma 2: Y ≪ X implies Y° ⊂ X°.

Purpose: build a point-free calculus of interiors and apartness for tame closed sets, as part of the 1986 Analysis situs axiomatics.
errors: Omb°°(X) ⊂ Omb(X)∖Omb(∂X) requires that no non-empty Y can be both apart from ∂X and ≪ ∂X. This fails if an empty or degenerate piece lies in M; the 'évidemment' tacitly assumes non-emptiness.
The ⇒ direction uses Omb(X') ⊂ Omb(X) for X' ∈ X̃. That is only justified if members of X̃ are ≤ X, which is not stated on this page; p.89 supplies it.
The ⇐ direction is not proved here, only attributed to L2 and L3. On p.89 Grothendieck changes his mind ('OK sans même Att L2, L3'), so the dependency on these axioms is uncertain.
The remark 'Z ≪ X,Y ⇒ ∃ Z' ∈ Z̃ with Z' < X or Z' < Y' is unclear and unmotivated as written.

ideas.what: Point-free interior: X° defined as the family of sub-pieces Y ≪ X that are apart from ∂X.
ideas.modern_name: Interior as an ideal of compact pieces way-below / non-tangentially inside X (round-ideal style; cf. RCC non-tangential proper part)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead/de Laguna/Clarke mereotopology; Scott's way-below relation in continuous lattices (1972); Randell-Cui-Cohn RCC (1992)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of tame topology appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this axiomatics is unpublished.

ideas.what: Apartness of interiors X° ‖ Y° as the absence of a common interior sub-piece; X ‖ Y characterised via interiors of all slight modifications X', Y'.
ideas.modern_name: Disconnection versus external connection (DC vs EC) in region-connection calculus, expressed point-free

ideas.what: Reduction of apartness to points (axioms L2, L3): X ‖ Y iff all points of X are apart from all points of Y.
ideas.where_published: Spirit of SGA4 'enough points', not this axiomatics

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics is a form of mereotopology / qualitative region calculus. Its primitives are pieces, inclusion ≤, a 'well inside' relation ≪, apartness ‖, boundary, and interiors defined as families of pieces strictly inside. It was developed independently of the Whitehead–Clarke–RCC tradition and of the continuous-lattice way-below formalism, and the literature does not seem to have compared them.
missed.quote: Omb°°(X) = { Y ∈ Omb(X) | Y ∥ ∂X } ... X° ∥ Y° ⟺ Omb°°(X) ∩ Omb°°(Y) = ∅
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could give a tame-topology (o-minimal / polyhedral) model theory of region calculi, tied to Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' programme. Some interest is plausible, but it is speculative.

missed.claim: The characterisation X ∥ Y ⇔ ∀X'∈X̃, Y'∈Ỹ, X'° ∥ Y'° is left unproved in the ⇐ direction. Its axiomatic status (needs L2, L3 or not) is unresolved between pp.88–89.
missed.quote: L'implication plus délicate est ⟸. Elle est conséquence de ArL2 et ArL3
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor; this is internal bookkeeping in an unfinished axiomatic system.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working page inside an unpublished point-free axiomatic tame topology. The definition of interior as a family of 'strictly inside' sub-pieces strongly parallels mereotopology and the way-below relation. That parallel is probably unremarked, but the page itself contains routine definitions and an unfinished lemma.
transcription_corrections: First line plausibly 'Faisons le point pour le moment des axiomes ...' rather than 'Faisons la structure'; uncertain.
'ArL2 et ArL3' should probably read 'AtL2 et AtL3' (axiom labels; p.89 has 'Att L2, L3').
In the last line, points are written with lowercase omb: '∀x ∈ omb(X), ∀y ∈ omb(Y), x ∥ y'.
Z ⊓ ∂X = ∅ is written with a meet-like symbol (⊓), not ∩.
